title: A substantial extremal theorem from exponent lattice orderings
objective: Achieve a substantial mathematical advance connected to the smooth-number exponent-lattice observations, with resolving a recognized quantitative problem as the success criterion rather than producing another manuscript. The concrete first target is the worst-case number G_3(n) of distinct monomial initial ideals of a length-n polynomial quotient in three variables, over all fields. Determine its sharp asymptotic growth, or prove an infinite realizable family with a polynomially larger number of orderings than the generic corner-cut scale, together with a consequential general theorem. Explain what algebraic dependencies add to the prime/smooth lattice geometry. First audit the strongest relevant primary literature and the repository's unfinished lattice-shadow work; distinguish a genuinely new theorem from a classical geometric corollary before using it. Success requires a complete uniform proof that settles this extremal question or a substantial recognized part of it, a rigorous consequence for algebraic or geometric complexity beyond restating the count, independently implemented reproducible supporting checks, and an honestly attributed paper. A draft, a bounded priority review, isolated examples, a minor refinement, or an unverified novelty claim cannot complete this goal. If this target is already settled or a route fails, record the evidence and choose a comparably consequential problem still directly linked to the original mathematics; do not silently lower the success criterion. Preserve all existing manuscripts, core smooth-number kernels and auditor, previous research, and the paused ML work. Never send emails, messages to people or other tasks, author queries, or submissions. Publish only explicitly privacy-reviewed research files to the already authorized main branch.
relationship_to_previous_work: New active objective with a higher completion bar. Previous goal records, lattice-shadow candidate, manuscripts and paused ML results are preserved as historical research.

definitions.G_d_n: Maximum number of monomial initial ideals of a colength-n ideal in d variables, over all fields.
definitions.F_d_n: The corresponding maximum for n distinct rational points; F_d(n) <= G_d(n).

success_criteria: Sharp asymptotic growth for G_3(n), or an infinite realizable family polynomially above the generic corner-cut scale together with a consequential general theorem.
A complete uniform proof settling the target or a substantial recognized part, and a further rigorous algebraic or geometric consequence beyond restating the count.
A current primary-source comparison establishing the exact novelty boundary; an unavailable paper does not establish novelty.
Independent reproducible supporting checks and an honestly attributed paper; acceptance and impact are not presumed.
A draft, isolated examples, a bounded search, a minor refinement or an unverified novelty claim cannot complete the goal.

A planar family with m^(1+epsilon) initial ideals would meet the three-variable power-separation part at exponent 2+2epsilon. Audit the strongest current planar bound and the exact fibre-product priority boundary, then prove or refute a proposed uniform planar mechanism before enlarging experiments. continuations.title: Local filtration bounds and a coherent coefficient distinction
continuations.previous_evidence: Commit f2c280c saved the active goal, source comparison and exact family diagnostics.
uniform_proofs: For every monomial basis of a finite algebra supported at one rational point, total degree is at most S=sum_j j*dim(m^j/m^(j+1)). Classical state geometry gives g(I)=O_d((1+S)^(d(d-1)/(d+1))).

For every nonlinear rectangle A_(r,s,F), n=rs, the coordinate moment budgets imply g(I)=O(n^(3/2)*sqrt((r-1)*(s-1)*(r+s-2))). Square rectangles therefore have g(I)=O(n^(9/4)), uniformly over all fields.
The fixed coefficient rule satisfies D*(z+4)-N=0 with D=(1-x)^3*(1-y)^2. Its universal leading monomial x^3*y^2*z is excluded in every initial standard set.
For every r>=8,s>=6, a 23-column ground subset is dependent for the fixed rule but has a unit minor for F=x+y+x^4*y^3. This proves genuine specialization relative to free coefficients.

For every a,b>=1,t nonzero, the embedding F=x+y+t*x^a*y^b in a 2a by 2b rectangle has an explicit coherent standard basis at weight (2,2,3). For a>=4,b>=3 it contains x^3*y^2*z, distinguishing actual initial ideals from the fixed probe.

independent_controls.moment_budgets: Every saved basis, plus all independent determinant bases in the length-4 exhaustive control.
independent_controls.unit_minor: Integer entrywise block-triangular verification; determinant 1, or t^12 with a parameter.
independent_controls.coherence_controls: Six relations replayed, strict leading inequalities and direct greedy residue ranks on the complete ground; no larger complete fans are enumerated.

continuations.priority_and_significance: The filtration estimate combines an elementary determinant argument with classical lattice vertex geometry. The other identities and one-cone construction are diagnostics. No novelty, sharpness, polynomial lower separation or unrestricted asymptotic advance is established.
continuations.effect_on_next_action: A count proof must distinguish the fixed rational surface from free-coefficient embeddings. The square family has at most a quarter-power window above the generic scale. Neither a larger matrix rank nor the one-cone witness establishes a larger fan.

continuations.title: Generic graph rank and coherent nongeneric dependencies
continuations.previous_evidence: Commit a2323c9 supplied uniform local moment bounds and a coherent distinction between coefficient embeddings.
uniform_proofs: For a finite abelian character table over a splitting field whose characteristic does not divide the group order, every maximal selection of character columns multiplied by independent row parameters to distinct nonnegative block powers has a nonzero generic determinant. Proof: transitive row matroids are uniformly dense; classical matroid partition gives a coefficient which cannot cancel.

For generic graph values above an r by s torus grid, all n=rs distinct canonical monomials with x exponent below r and y exponent below s are independent. Its initial standard sets are exactly ordinary positive n-cuts of the canonical exponent strip.

Any uniform-cut route on at most n*(1+log n)^2 exponent points yielding n^(2+epsilon) standard sets would yield M^(2+epsilon-o(1)) balanced strict halfspace subsets of a general-position three-dimensional configuration. The padding proof keeps M between N and 2N.

For every q>=3 and every local square graph with nonzero x and y linear coefficients, in characteristic zero or characteristic greater than 2q-2, a prescribed positive-weight first-n nonzero prefix is dependent: z^(2q-2)=2*beta*y*z^(2q-3) is a nonzero parallel pair inside it.

independent_controls.method: Direct permutation expansion in formal row parameters; the base Fourier matrices have zero smaller minors. No random scalar evaluation is used.

continuations.literature_boundary: Uniform density and matroid partition are credited published inputs. The geometric padding comparison concerns only families already reducible to ordinary cuts. A 2026 proposed planar improvement remains an uninspected source lead.
continuations.effect_on_next_action: Avoid generic torus-grid graph searches as an easy route to polynomial amplification. The local algebra family is not covered by that uniform-cut reduction, and the saved small fans already refute confinement of rank defects to coordinate-face bases. A quantitative theorem about overlapping coherent dependencies in interior weight regions is still needed.
continuations.claim_limit: No polynomial fan-count separation, new unrestricted asymptotic, algorithmic speedup, novelty certificate or paper-level significance is established.

continuations.uniform_control: For n_q=q(q+1)/2+floor((q+1)/2), a connected Johnson graph of at least 2^(q+1)/(q+2) standard-set candidates has every edge realized by a length-n_q binomial ideal over every field. At most two candidates can be initial bases of any one fixed ideal, because their state vectors are collinear. This is an elementary classical-state-geometry control, not an asserted new extremal theorem.

continuations.effect_on_next_action: Derive a quantitative bound on simultaneous coherent basis changes using the common quotient and global state geometry, or construct an infinite realizable family with a proved growth rate. Published T-graph arrow-map constraints concern individual pairs and do not supply this count: an explicit connected shell graph has exponentially many individually realizable vertices but at most two can occur in one fan. The published generic-uniformity theorem also requires the standard grading; its positive nonstandard variants fail even after removing loops and coloops. Do not enlarge finite fan sizes without a discriminating quantitative hypothesis or lower the original success criterion.

continuations.uniform_theorem: For planar ideals J_i with common monic f(x) in every J_i, H=(f, y_i*y_j for i<j, y_i*J_i(x,y_i)) has length deg(f)+sum length(J_i). For every global order, in(H)=(x^deg(f), y_i*y_j, y_i*in(J_i)). Every branch fan combination is realized by independently normalizing its positive x weight to one, so g(H)=product g(J_i), over every field.
continuations.extremal_consequence: Cayley--Hamilton supplies a degree-m f for any length-m planar quotient. With d-1 copies, G_d(d*m)>=G_2(m)^(d-1); in particular G_3(3m)>=G_2(m)^2. A planar m^(1+epsilon) lower family would yield the original spatial power separation. No such planar family is established.
further_consequences: The positive fan is a product in the independent ratios w_yi/w_x.
The explicit universal Groebner basis has at most 1+binom(r,2)+sum |U(J_i)| elements.

The same extremal transfer holds for arbitrary reduced rational point sets: F_d(d*m)>=F_2(m)^(d-1). After an infinite extension if necessary, translate the second coordinate away from zero and choose a squarefree degree-m x annihilator by padding distinct axis roots. No separating first coordinate or smoothing is assumed.
